# Switch NX2 - read when the Lichii GUI starts.
# One NAME=VALUE per line. Lines starting with # are ignored.
# A variable already set in the environment wins over this file.
# Between files, the user copy (%APPDATA%\eglantine\nx2_switches.txt, or
# $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/eglantine/nx2_switches.txt; in a portable build user\nx2_switches.txt, or
# user/config/nx2_switches.txt) wins over this one, so editing this file is never
# needed: copy the lines you want into your own and restart.
#
# Restart the emulator after editing.

# --- Performance tuning defaults for Switch 2 ---
# Offload GPU method/macro execution to the back thread (SPLIT=2 delivers up to +54% FPS alone).
EDEN_NX2_SPLIT=2

# Batch GPU fence syncpoints to reduce host driver overhead and smooth frametimes.
EDEN_NX2_FENCE_BATCH=1

# Leave buffer downloads disabled on Switch 2 (default): forcing downloads (=1) copies back
# 90-220 MB/s of buffers CPU never touches, causing heavy mutex contention and dropping FPS by ~38-63%.
#EDEN_NX2_BUFFER_DOWNLOADS=1

# Paces frame submission 2 frames ahead. Reduces frametime spikes, but adds ~1-2 frames of input latency.
# Enable only if frame pacing stability is preferred over responsive controls.
#EDEN_NX2_FRAMES_AHEAD=2

# --- Workarounds / Debug ---
# Terrain/indirect drawing fix for Donkey Kong Bananza: enabled by default. Set to 0 only to leave to GPU.
#EDEN_NX2_RESETFIX=0

# Drop reactive-flushing read traps on Switch 2 programs (opt-in; can reduce FPS from 29 to 24 in MKW).
#EDEN_NX2_NO_REACTIVE=1

# Graphics pipelines linked from per-stage shader libraries (VK_EXT_graphics_pipeline_library with
# fast linking; not on MoltenVK). Off by default; EDEN_NX2_GPL_FAST_LINK=0 links optimized.
#EDEN_NX2_GPL=1

# With EDEN_NX2_GPL=1 and "Precache shaders before game start": the game's vertex and fragment
# programs are also prepared (rebuild the precache after setting it). Ocarina of Time: a 1.5 GB
# file, six more minutes on the first loading screen, 2.3 GB of driver cache; pop-in ends sooner,
# frame times are the same as with the compute precache alone.
#EDEN_NX2_GRAPHICS_PRECACHE=1

# Ocarina of Time with the "AMD FSR 3.1" anti-aliasing choice: 0 draws the scene without the
# per-frame sub-pixel offset FSR is given.
#EDEN_NX2_OOT_JITTER=0

# Ocarina of Time with NVIDIA DLSS (or MetalFX temporal): 1 gives it the same sub-pixel offset,
# 2 with the vertical sign flipped. Experiment, off by default.
#EDEN_NX2_DLSS_JITTER=1

# Ocarina of Time: 1 draws the game's upscale pass as one bilinear tap whenever no temporal
# upscaler takes the frame (phones get it from their device profile; 0 turns it off there).
#EDEN_NX2_OOT_BILINEAR_UPSCALE=1

# Ocarina of Time handheld: 1 lets DLSS / FSR 3.1 take the upscale from the lower scales to
# 1920x1080 (on by default on Apple for MetalFX temporal, 0 turns it off).
#EDEN_NX2_OOT_TEMPORAL_HANDHELD=1

# Ocarina of Time: the 3D scene's size for tests, over the "Resolution" setting (oot_resolution):
# 1 = 75%, 2 = 56%, 3 = 50%, 4 = 40% (768x432 handheld), 5 = 1/3 (640x360 handheld; docked it is
# 40%, since a third of 2560x1440 is padded and drawn twice). The finished picture stays 1920x1080
# handheld. Each change of a frame's sizes writes one "Frame chain:" line.
#EDEN_NX2_OOT_RENDER_SCALE=4

# A draw without render targets (it writes buffers or counts samples only) gets a render pass as
# large as its scissors reach instead of the surface clip (Ocarina of Time leaves that at
# 32768x32768). On by default on Apple, where the GPU prepares every tile of it; 0 turns it off.
#EDEN_NX2_TARGETLESS_REACH=1

# Streamed uniform buffers on MoltenVK: static (default) pads to the shader's used size unless it
# indexes the buffer; readable also zero-fills indexed ones to 64 KiB, bank always 64 KiB, poison
# fills with 0xff the shader can see (finds reads past the guest's size), 0 none.
#EDEN_NX2_UBO_PAD=static

# 0: a fence release submits deferred GPU work only when its callback has not run (something
# waits). Phones get 0 from their device profile.
#EDEN_NX2_RELEASE_SUBMIT=1

# The split GPU thread, out of commands with a deferred submission younger than
# EDEN_NX2_FENCE_FLUSH_US, waits up to this many us for more work first (it spins meanwhile).
#EDEN_NX2_IDLE_GRACE_US=0

# The same wait asleep, and only while the GPU still runs work submitted earlier (it has no use
# for another command buffer yet): up to this many us, ended by new work, by a thread asking for
# the submission or by the GPU running dry (the idea of nxnative PR #2645). 0 = off.
# EDEN_NX2_IDLE_HOLD_ANY=1 holds whatever the GPU does, to measure it on a PC. Phones get 500
# from their device profile (PC phone sim: idle submits 3.0 -> 0.9 a frame, 21.1 -> 19.6 command
# buffers, frame rate unchanged).
#EDEN_NX2_IDLE_HOLD_US=0

# The two GPU threads sleep on each other in the OS's address wait (WaitOnAddress, Apple
# os_sync_wait_on_address) instead of std::atomic::wait, which on Apple polls and yields for up
# to 64 us before it sleeps. 0 = std::atomic::wait.
#EDEN_NX2_SPLIT_ADDRESS_WAIT=1

# 0: the GPU thread polling its suspended channels and a thread waiting for a deferred submission
# sleep 50 us between polls instead of yielding. Phones get 0 from their device profile: Apple's
# sched_yield (swtch_pri) runs the caller at priority 0 for up to 10 ms when anything else is
# runnable, and spins on its core when nothing is. (On Windows a 50 us sleep lasts a timer tick.)
# Also the other short polls: the frame limiter's and present hold's last millisecond, a guest
# write waiting for a GPU download to land, the 200 us wait for a background pipeline, the GPU
# memory page table's 2 ms try-lock, a full split ring, a busy fiber, the IPC reply hold, a new
# guest thread's start, and a GPU unmap waiting for deferred page protection changes.
#EDEN_NX2_POLL_YIELD=1

# Graphics thread cuts from zortos293/Lichii (each on by default; 0 turns one back):
# QUERY_CUTS (#1515): report ids taken from the free list a batch at a time, finished reports
# freed a streamer at a time outside the cache lock, small report lookups probe the offsets a
# report can start at, and pages no report was ever on are skipped without the lock.
# FENCE_CUTS (#1516): a new fence wakes the fencing thread only when it waits for fences, and
# occlusion report lists are kept for reuse.
# PROTECT_UNLOCKED (#1518): page untracking caused by a guest CPU write (a protection system call
# per run) runs after the buffer cache's lock is dropped; GPU unmaps wait for it.
# WORDS_POOL (#1520): the submit-time copies of command lists come from a pool of kept blocks
# (at most 4 MiB a size class) instead of the heap.
# RESUME_PUBLISH (#1520): at a resumed semaphore acquire, what the front decoded goes to the back
# before the waiting lists are copied again.
# COLLECT_SPLIT (#1586): a guest write crossing a 2 KiB page is collected a page at a time (one
# transform could not hold it and lost part of it).
# USAGE_RESET_BOUNDED (#1586): a buffer's per-frame usage words are cleared only where set.
#EDEN_NX2_QUERY_CUTS=1
#EDEN_NX2_FENCE_CUTS=1
#EDEN_NX2_PROTECT_UNLOCKED=1
#EDEN_NX2_WORDS_POOL=1
#EDEN_NX2_RESUME_PUBLISH=1
#EDEN_NX2_COLLECT_SPLIT=1
#EDEN_NX2_USAGE_RESET_BOUNDED=1

# Apple: frame threads tell the kernel how much CPU time they need each frame
# (THREAD_TIME_CONSTRAINT_POLICY, measured over 120 frames; port of nxnative PR #2569 / #2137).
# A sum of 1 = GPUBack, 2 = GPU, 4 = VulkanWorker, 8 = the guest cores. iPhone and iPad: 7 by
# default; macOS 0. "frame deadlines:" in the Perf host CPU line shows what each declared and how
# often the kernel took it out of the real-time band.
#EDEN_NX2_APPLE_FRAME_DEADLINE=0

# The fencing thread lets a deferred fence submission wait this many us after the fence was
# made before it asks the GPU thread for it (0 = at once).
#EDEN_NX2_FENCE_PATIENCE_US=0

# An emulated mesh draw inside a render pass that began on a command buffer of its own runs its
# compute just before that pass instead of ending and reopening it (when no draw of the pass stored
# to memory and it samples none of the pass's targets). 0 ends the pass as before.
#EDEN_NX2_MESH_BEFORE_PASS=1

# MoltenVK: a guest dispatch right after another one (only bindings between) records no barrier,
# so both share one serial Metal compute encoder (a barrier ends it). Off by default; force applies
# it on every driver, for tests only (not valid Vulkan).
#EDEN_NX2_DISPATCH_CHAIN=1

# Mesh pipelines the driver could build natively take the compute emulation instead: all, or a
# comma list of pipeline hashes. To compare the two (Apple mesh shaders are occupancy bound).
#EDEN_NX2_MESH_EMULATE=all

# Diagnostic: every 10 s a "Dispatch deps" line names the compute dispatches that end an open
# render pass, and whether they bind its images or follow storage writes in it. Draws nothing
# differently.
#EDEN_NX2_DISPATCH_DEPS=1

# Metal renderer: 0 writes no log line for a SIGABRT or an uncaught Objective-C exception (Metal
# aborts the process on a descriptor or call it rejects; the line names the thread and frames).
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_ABORT_TRACE=0

# Metal renderer: 0 makes command buffers without per-encoder status, so a failed one logs its
# error without the encoders that did not complete.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_ENCODER_STATUS=0

# Metal renderer: programs are translated with the draw's fixed state as on Vulkan: depth -1..1
# converted in the vertex program, point size written for point lists, the alpha test in the pixel
# program, dual source blending outputs, pixel outputs typed after integer targets, lower left
# window origin. 0 translates them without, as before.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_FIXED_STATE=0

# Either renderer: counts what the game asks of the graphics backend (draw state by pipeline,
# clears, dispatches, queries, translated programs, images, views, samplers, copies) and writes
# it every 10 s to nx2_feature_census.json in the log folder. tools/nx2/feature_census.py prints
# it; tools/nx2/metal_replay reads it. Draws nothing differently.
#EDEN_NX2_FEATURE_CENSUS=1

# Metal renderer: 0 hands Metal the guest's vertex layout, pipeline and texture descriptions as
# they are, as before. Metal aborts the process on some (a 32nd vertex stream or attribute, an
# attribute of a stream without a buffer, a sample count a texture can't have, a texture past its
# size limit, alpha to coverage on an integer target); by default the vertex layout is rewritten
# to what the vertex program reads and what is left over is refused with a "refused:" log line,
# the draw skipped; alpha to coverage is left off on an integer target; a pass without
# attachments says it has one sample per pixel; a buffer, texture or sampler slot past a stage's
# tables is not bound; 1D images are kept as 2D textures a texel high and shaders read them as
# such, as on MoltenVK (Metal's 1D textures take no mip levels and no 2D views); a texture view
# of another family of texture types, with a slice count its type can't have or in a format Metal
# doesn't cast to is refused with a "refused:" log line, as is a 1D or 3D texture in a depth or
# stencil format. The same switch holds the checks Metal makes only in its validation layer,
# which release builds lack: a buffer bound at an offset past its end is bound as zeros, an
# attachment's level or slice past its texture becomes the last one, an attachment whose format
# or sample count the pipeline lacks takes the texture's format of the same kind or is left out;
# the stencil views the scheduler's blits make are checked as texture views are; a guest target
# of more samples than the GPU has (8 on Apple GPUs) is drawn at the GPU's most; and a refused
# render pipeline is drawn again without blending and alpha to coverage, a refused or missing
# texture reads zeros. Each is counted on the `Perf Metal coverage:` line as `guards: <name>
# <count>` and logged once as `Metal: guard: ...`.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_PIPELINE_CHECK=0

# Metal renderer: guest reads, guest writes and the GPU's inline writes take the paths the
# Vulkan renderer takes: a cache that can hold nothing of a range is not asked (no wait for its
# lock: EDEN_NX2_READ_FASTPATH, EDEN_NX2_TEXTURE_READ_FILTER, EDEN_NX2_WRITE_FASTPATH), a guest
# write that finds the buffer cache's lock held is handed to the lock's owner
# (EDEN_NX2_WRITE_HANDOFF), collected guest writes are applied in one batch and pages they
# replace stop being held GPU-modified (EDEN_NX2_CPU_WRITE_RECLAIM), a guest read of GPU data
# still on its way waits for the copy under way on its own core (EDEN_NX2_GPU_READ_LAND), a
# fence release with nothing to release does not drain the GPU thread (EDEN_NX2_EXP3), and
# inline writes go straight to guest memory with one invalidation before the next draw
# (EDEN_NX2_INLINE_FAST, EDEN_NX2_INLINE_DEFER, EDEN_NX2_I2M_COALESCE, EDEN_NX2_I2M_LIST_PAGE);
# each of those switches works as on Vulkan. 0 takes the plain paths this renderer had before:
# every question under both caches' locks, writes applied one at a time, reads landed by the GPU
# thread, every fence release drained, every inline write invalidating every cache at once.
# Under it, as on Vulkan: every draw serves the guest threads' waiting sync requests, a draw
# whose native program failed marks the frame as such, and Donkey Kong Bananza's reset program
# has its indirect records written on the host (EDEN_NX2_RESETFIX). A draw count the GPU wrote
# (EDEN_NX2_INDIRECT_DRAWS=1) is read back before the draw, which waits for the GPU; a draw of
# more than 16 million vertices is skipped with a log line under EDEN_NX2_METAL_PIPELINE_CHECK.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_CACHE_PATHS=0

# Metal renderer: 0 translates programs with SPIRV-Cross's settings for any iOS device, as
# before: a program that reads the base instance or base vertex (every vertex program that reads
# the instance index) is refused and its draws skipped, and subgroup operations work on groups
# of four pixels. By default the translation is told what the GPU has, as MoltenVK tells it:
# base vertex and instance (Apple3 and later), SIMD groups for subgroup operations (Apple6 and
# later), the cube map gradient fix, no stores from discarded fragments, and an input structure
# that contains itself declared as a pointer (Metal 3.1's compiler does not return from it).
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_MSL_DEVICE=0

# Metal renderer: 0 skips two kinds of image copy, as before. By default a blit from a depth
# image into a depth image is drawn (nearest; the stencil comes along between images of one
# format), and a copy between a block-compressed image and a plain one whose texels are the
# size of a block goes through a buffer, block for texel, as Vulkan copies them (Ocarina of
# Time copies R16G16B16A16_UINT into BC4). A copy that starts inside a block is skipped with a
# log line either way; images decoded on the CPU are not copied this way. The same switch covers
# depth and stencil data: 24-bit depth, depth with stencil and stencil images are uploaded and
# downloaded in the guest's bytes (a draw writes depth and stencil from the buffer, a kernel
# reads them back: Metal has no 24-bit depth and no blit copy of packed depth-stencil), Vulkan's
# depth <-> colour conversions (ABGR8 <-> D24S8 / S8D24 / X8D24 / D32F, D32F -> R32F, D16 <->
# R16) are drawn, depth images are reinterpreted through a buffer, and resolution scaling scales
# stencil-only images with a draw exporting the stencil. With 0 all of them are skipped, as before.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_COPIES=0

# Metal renderer: 0 makes one sampler state per guest sampler, as before: no LOD bias and no
# min / max reduction, the OpenGL clamp clamps to the edge and both mirror-once modes Metal
# lacks clamp without the mirrored repeat. By default the guest's LOD bias (plus the Ocarina
# upscaler's, as Vulkan's) and reduction are set where the SDK and OS have them (macOS / iOS 26;
# older systems log once and sample without), the OpenGL clamp reaches the border when the
# guest filters, the mirror-once modes mirror once and clamp to the edge, and a view gets a
# variant of the sampler where Vulkan uses another one: no added anisotropy for views that take
# none, nearest for integer views, no comparison for plain reads, the sRGB border colour for
# sRGB views. Metal has three fixed border colours: a guest border colour is the nearest of them.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_SAMPLERS=0

# Metal renderer: 0 leaves multisampled images as before: never uploaded, downloaded or copied
# to or from single-sampled images, blits from them dropped, and a program reading one as a plain
# texture given the multisampled texture. By default a multisampled image keeps a single-sampled
# texture holding its samples as texels, as the guest lays them out, filled and drained by a draw
# per layer: uploads and downloads go through it, CopyImageMSAA draws between the two, a program
# that reads the image as a plain texture reads it, and blits resolve (Metal's resolve store
# action for a whole image, the samples scaled into the rectangle otherwise), and resolution
# scaling scales colour and depth ones sample for sample with a draw (Metal blits no multisampled
# texture). Multisampled stencil is not copied or scaled (Metal writes no stencil per sample from a
# fragment).
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_MSAA=0

# Metal renderer: 0 makes no texture for R32G32B32_FLOAT (Metal has no 96-bit format) and reads
# G4R4_UNORM as R8 (only the high nibble survives), as before. By default both are expanded on
# the CPU at upload, into RGBA32Float (alpha 1) and RG8Unorm (red from the high nibble, as
# Vulkan's R4G4_UNORM_PACK8); texel buffers of them keep the guest's bytes.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_FORMATS=0

# Metal renderer: 0 stores every attachment of every pass, as before. By default, on Apple GPUs, an
# attachment a pass loads and no draw of the pass can write (colour write mask 0, depth and stencil
# writes off) is not stored again (MTLStoreActionDontCare); nxnative's unwritten-attachment rule.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_UNWRITTEN_STORE=0

# Metal renderer: 0 makes large images over Switch 2 sparse regions whole, as before. By default,
# with tier 2 sparse textures (Apple6+, OS 26), such an image is a texture of a sparse heap mapped
# by tile as the guest memory under it can hold data. EDEN_NX2_METAL_SPARSE_MIB=<n> sets the
# heap's size (default an eighth of the image, 16 to 256 MiB).
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_SPARSE=0

# Metal renderer: 0 gives a render pass the bound slice of each attachment only, as before: a
# program that picks the layer (its layer output) draws into the first. By default a pass of a
# layered framebuffer has renderTargetArrayLength set to the fewest layers among its attachments'
# views (array and cube textures; a 3D slice or a plain 2D texture keeps one), as Vulkan's
# framebuffer layers.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_LAYERS=0

# Metal renderer: 0 binds a storage buffer whose guest range spans several mappings at its first
# mapping, as before (what lies past it is read from the wrong place). By default such a binding,
# when the program only reads it, gets its segments copied into one buffer before the draw or
# dispatch, as Vulkan's gathered multi-range fallback; written ones stay on the plain path (Metal
# has no sparse buffer aliasing here, as Vulkan without sparse binding).
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_MULTI_RANGE=0

# Metal renderer: 0 clears as before: a clear of part of a target (the scissor), of some colour
# channels or of some stencil bits clears the whole target, every channel and every bit, and a
# whole-number colour target takes the clear colour's floats. By default such a clear is drawn
# as a triangle over the rectangle with the channels' and bits' write masks (a clear of the
# whole target stays the render pass's load action), and whole-number targets get the values
# Vulkan gives them. Ocarina of Time clears with the scissor test on about 1,600 times a second
# on a computer (how many of them cover less than the target was not measured).
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_CLEAR_DRAWS=0

# Metal renderer: 0 gives every clear of a whole target a render pass of its own, as before
# (the pass stores the cleared image and the pass with the draws loads it again). By default
# the clear waits and becomes the load action of the next render pass when that pass draws
# into the same images, as Vulkan's renderer defers its clears; a pass on other images, a
# dispatch, a blit, a copy that touches one of the images, a present or a flush records the
# clear first. The 10 s "Metal:" line counts the passes "starting with a clear".
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_CLEAR_FOLD=0

# Metal renderer: 0 ignores the game's fragment barrier, as before: a draw that samples the
# image its own render pass draws into reads what the pass before it stored. By default the
# next draw after a barrier that samples one of its targets (or follows a draw that writes
# storage) ends the render pass first, so the image holds the earlier draws, and opens it
# again; other draws stay in the open pass, as on Vulkan (EDEN_NX2_WFI_DEFER). The 10 s
# "Metal:" line counts the passes ended this way. The same holds for a depth feedback loop (a
# draw sampling the depth image its pass writes, the texture cache's barrier_feedback_loops
# check): the pass ends before it, counted as "guards: depth feedback loop pass ends".
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_FRAGMENT_BARRIER=0

# Metal renderer: 0 sets every piece of state (pipeline, depth-stencil state, viewport,
# scissor, culling, depth bias, stencil references, blend colour) and every buffer, texture and
# sampler again for each draw and dispatch, as before. By default what the open encoder already
# has stays as it is, and a buffer bound again at another offset only gets the offset. The
# 10 s "Metal:" line counts state and bindings set and left as they were.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_STATE_CACHE=0

# Metal renderer: 0 records the buffer cache's uploads and the kernels of a draw (index
# rewrite, mesh and tessellation emulation) where they come, as before: each ends the open
# render pass, and the draw opens it again (the pass stores its images and loads them). By
# default they go into two command buffers of their own, committed before the one with the
# passes, as Vulkan's renderer records its uploads and its mesh compute before the pass: an
# upload when nothing recorded since the last commit uses the bytes, a kernel when the pass it
# belongs to is the first thing recorded since then and has not written storage (a mesh or
# tessellation kernel also not when the draw writes storage or samples its own targets). The
# 10 s "Metal:" line counts the copies and kernels "ahead of their segment".
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_AHEAD=0

# Metal renderer: 0 commits nothing early for the sake of the above. By default a render pass
# whose kernels had to end it (because other work came before the pass since the last commit)
# has that earlier work committed just before it begins the next time, at most 8 times between
# two flushes, so its kernels can go ahead of it. The 10 s "Metal:" line counts the
# "segments split off".
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_AHEAD_SPLIT=0

# Metal renderer: 0 commits a command buffer for every guest fence (syncpoint increments, query
# and download fences), also when nothing was recorded since the last commit, as before. By
# default such a fence waits for the last command buffer committed and makes none, as Vulkan's
# renderer does. The 10 s "Metal:" line counts the "fences without a command buffer".
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_FENCE_IDLE=0

# Metal renderer: 0 leaves its pool of staging buffers (texture and buffer uploads, downloads)
# without bounds, as before: every upload past the stream ring takes a buffer of its own until
# the command buffer is committed, and a free buffer is given back only after 300 frames and
# only from the end of the list. By default the pool has the Vulkan renderer's two marks
# (EDEN_NX2_STAGING_SUBMIT_MIB, EDEN_NX2_STAGING_CAP_MIB: 24 and 96 MiB on phones, 256 and 1024
# elsewhere): before a draw, clear or dispatch the command buffer being recorded is committed
# once the buffers it took pass the first; with more than the second held the GPU thread waits
# for it and frees buffers down to half the cap; and while more than the first mark is held a
# free buffer goes after 8 frames. The 10 s "Metal:" line reports the pool ("staging").
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_STAGING_BOUND=0

# Metal renderer: 0 lets Ocarina of Time's anti-aliasing network run whatever the "Ocarina of
# Time anti-aliasing" setting says, as before. By default, with that setting at No sharpening,
# the network's passes are skipped and its output pass is replaced by a copy of the tonemapped
# image, as on Vulkan (docs/nx2/oot-network-bypass.md).
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_NETWORK_BYPASS=0

# Metal renderer: 0 writes no pipeline files and builds nothing before play, as before: every
# program is translated and compiled on the draw's thread at its first use in each run, and its
# MSL text is kept for the session. By default each pipeline a run makes is recorded in the
# game's shader directory (metal.fork-v1.bin: its programs, as Vulkan's cache; metal_states.bin:
# the render states Metal made from it; metal_used.bin: which pipelines the last runs used), and
# the next boot translates and builds them on worker threads (the pipeline archive then gives
# the GPU code), the pipelines used in the last 8 runs only once a used list exists. The MSL
# text is freed once its function is built. 2 builds every recorded pipeline at boot. A boot
# build that did not finish (the process died in it) is skipped by the next run.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_PIPELINE_FILE=0

# Metal renderer: 0 leaves Ocarina of Time's upscale pass to the bilinear pass or the game, as
# before, also with the upscaler set to MetalFX Temporal. By default, with that setting (or
# EDEN_NX2_DLSS_REPLACEMENT=dlss), the pass is replaced as on Vulkan: the camera is read from the
# scene draws, motion is made from the scene depth, MetalFX upscales and the game's target is
# written from its output; EDEN_NX2_OOT_TEMPORAL_HANDHELD applies as on Vulkan.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_OOT_TEMPORAL=0

# Metal renderer: 0 draws flat inputs from each primitive's first vertex, as Metal (it has no
# provoking vertex setting) and MoltenVK draw them. By default a draw whose pixel program reads
# flat inputs while the game asks for the last vertex's values has its indices rewritten (by a
# kernel, or on the CPU for indices only in guest memory) so each primitive starts with the
# vertex Vulkan's last vertex convention takes them from, keeping the winding: lists, strips
# (with restart indices too, degenerate triangles across a restart), fans, quads, quad strips,
# lines, line strips and loops.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_PROVOKING_LAST=0

# Metal renderer: 0 translates and builds a pipeline first seen during a run on the draw's
# thread, which waits, as before. By default it is built on builder threads (this many; default
# logical CPUs - 1): a draw that may be skipped (EDEN_NX2_ASYNC_DISCARD, as Vulkan's
# DrawMayBeSkipped) is skipped meanwhile, one that may not runs an unstarted build itself or
# lends a running one its QoS class, as EDEN_NX2_PIPELINE_HOLD_BOOST on Vulkan. Vulkan's
# EDEN_NX2_ASYNC_TRANSLATE other than 1 turns it off too, and EDEN_NX2_ASYNC_TRANSLATE_THREADS
# sets the thread count when this one is not set.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_ASYNC_PIPELINES=0

# Metal renderer: 0 decides conditional rendering on the CPU from guest memory only (a pending
# occlusion report reads as what memory held). By default a condition on a report whose fence
# has not signalled is decided by a kernel after the counting passes, which zeroes the instance
# counts of the draws under it (drawn through indirect arguments); clears, indirect, mesh and
# tessellated draws under it wait for the report on the CPU. Metal has no predicated rendering.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_GPU_CONDITION=0

# Metal renderer: 0 reads an indirect draw's count from guest memory on the CPU and refuses
# indirect draws whose indices must be rewritten (8-bit, quads, fans, loops, the provoking
# vertex), and reads the vertex count of draws GPU work wrote (EDEN_NX2_INDIRECT_DRAWS) on the
# CPU, as before. By default kernels pack the arguments (draws past the count draw no instances),
# rewrite each draw's indices sized from its arguments, and build the plain draws' arguments.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_GPU_INDIRECT=0

# Metal renderer: 0 refuses DrawTexture, as before. By default it is a scaled blit of the
# texture's rectangle into colour target 0, filtered as its sampler's magnification filter.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_DRAW_TEXTURE=0

# Metal renderer: 0 clears only the bound layer of layered targets, as before. By default a
# clear covers the layers it names (its first layer and layer count).
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_CLEAR_LAYERS=0

# Metal renderer: 0 reads command lists the GPU wrote after a full sync and flush of their page,
# as before. By default, as on Vulkan, the pages a dispatch or DMA copy wrote are copied after it
# and the split's front reads the copies.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_LIST_COPIES=0

# Metal renderer: 0 sets viewport and scissor 0 only, as before. By default a draw whose vertex
# program writes the viewport index gets all 16.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_VIEWPORTS=0

# Metal renderer: 0 fills every triangle, as before. By default triangles whose drawn faces are
# in line polygon mode are drawn as their edges (Metal's line fill mode; it has no point mode,
# and one mode for both faces).
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_FILL_LINES=0

# Metal renderer: 0 ignores the base vertex of indexed tessellated draws, as before. By default
# it is added to their indices.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_TESS_BASE_VERTEX=0

# Metal renderer: 0 leaves alpha to one off, as before. By default pipelines take it from the
# game's state (Metal's alphaToOneEnabled; not on integer targets).
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_ALPHA_TO_ONE=0

# Metal renderer: 0 draws every task/mesh pipeline through the compute emulation, as before. By
# default, on a GPU with Metal 3 mesh pipelines (Apple7 and later, Mac2 with Metal 3), the task
# program becomes an object function and the mesh program a mesh function
# (MTLMeshRenderPipelineDescriptor, drawMeshThreadgroups); indirect mesh draws have their guest
# records rewritten into Metal's threadgroup counts by a kernel. A pipeline past Metal's mesh
# limits (256 vertices, 512 primitives, 16 KiB payload, 1024 threads, 32 KiB threadgroup memory),
# one whose functions or render state Metal refuses (logged once as "not drawn natively"), and
# every pipeline on a GPU without mesh pipelines take the emulation as before.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_MESH_NATIVE=0

# Metal renderer: 1 builds natively also mesh programs that write per-primitive attributes. Off by
# default: they take the emulation, as Vulkan does on MoltenVK, where the iPhone's compiler
# refused such a mesh function (Ocarina of Time's pipeline bbfd9d39350cdaaa).
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_MESH_PER_PRIMITIVE=1

# Metal renderer: 0 reads a task count the GPU wrote on the CPU before the draw (which waits for
# the GPU), as before. By default a natively drawn mesh pipeline takes the count from the GPU's
# copy of it (drawMeshThreadgroupsWithIndirectBuffer); emulated pipelines still read it.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_MESH_FROM_GPU=0

# Metal renderer: 0 refuses draws of lines, line strips, triangles and triangle strips with
# adjacency, as before ("topology Metal can't draw"). By default their indices are rewritten as
# Vulkan draws them without a geometry program: the adjacent vertices left out (Metal has no
# adjacency topologies).
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_ADJACENCY=0

# Metal renderer: 0 reads integer and scaled 10:10:10:2 attributes through Metal's normalized
# 10:10:10:2 formats, as before (wrong values). By default a kernel widens such an attribute into
# a buffer of its own as four 16-bit integers, which the vertex program reads as the guest's
# integers (Metal has 10:10:10:2 vertex formats only normalized).
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_VERTEX_UNPACK=0

# Metal renderer: 0 refuses a draw that reads more vertex streams than Metal has buffer slots
# next to the vertex program's own buffers, as before. By default the last free slot holds a
# buffer the attributes of the remaining per-vertex streams are copied into by a kernel before
# the draw (Metal has 31 buffer slots per stage); instanced and constant streams past the slots
# are still refused.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_VERTEX_GATHER=0

# Metal renderer: 0 gives Link's pixels the camera's motion only under the above, as before. By
# default his skinned draw's pose is kept for this frame and the last (bones, origin, mesh), and
# his mesh is drawn with both poses over the camera's motion where it lands on the scene depth,
# as Vulkan's ActorOverlay does (ocarina_actor_motion.vert/.frag through the translator). The
# "Ocarina MetalFX:" line counts the frames with "Link's motion".
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_OOT_ACTOR=0

# Metal renderer: 0 gives MetalFX no reactive mask under the above, as before. By default the
# scene is copied once the fog is drawn, the pixels the glows and particles change after it are
# marked when the game's next pass writes the scene, and the mark (with last frame's, moved) is
# MetalFX's reactive mask, so those pixels take this frame's colour, as on Vulkan. MetalFX takes
# a reactive mask from iOS 18 and macOS 15 on; before, none is made. The "Ocarina MetalFX:" line
# counts the frames with an "effects mask".
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_OOT_EFFECTS=0

# Metal renderer: the bits of float depth Link's replayed pixels may differ from the scene depth
# by under EDEN_NX2_METAL_OOT_ACTOR, 16 as on Vulkan. 4294967295 compares nothing (his whole
# mesh gets his motion, also where the scene hides him).
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_OOT_ACTOR_TOLERANCE=16

# Metal renderer: 0 ignores the Vulkan renderer's switches Metal reads, as before. By default the
# Metal renderer does what these do on Vulkan: EDEN_NX2_DYNSTATE_CACHE, EDEN_NX2_VERTEX_INPUT_CACHE,
# EDEN_NX2_STREAM_BUFFER_MIB, EDEN_NX2_FENCE_FLUSH_US (2000 on phones from the device profile),
# EDEN_NX2_FLUSH_DRAWS, EDEN_NX2_NO_MESH, EDEN_NX2_NO_MESH_FILE, EDEN_NX2_NO_MESH_EMULATION,
# EDEN_NX2_FORCE_LOD0, EDEN_NX2_PASS_TIMES, EDEN_NX2_DLSS_JITTER, EDEN_NX2_OOT_VISUAL_WORKAROUND,
# EDEN_NX2_TEMPORAL_WEIGHT, _KERNEL, _CLIP, _CLIP_MOTION, _KERNEL_MOTION and _SHARPEN,
# EDEN_NX2_BINDMEMO, _BATCH and _PARTIAL, EDEN_NX2_HOST_PACE, EDEN_NX2_PIPELINE_EVICT_LEFT_MIB
# and _MAX (docs/nx2/metal-coverage.md, section Q). Unset, the ones on by default on Vulkan
# (binding memo, host pacing) are on, with the Metal switches below to turn them off alone, and
# EDEN_NX2_FENCE_FLUSH_US and EDEN_NX2_PIPELINE_EVICT_LEFT_MIB take the phone profile's values.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_VULKAN_SWITCHES=0

# Metal renderer: 0 resolves every texture and image binding of each draw and dispatch again
# (FillImageViews, GetSamplerId), as before. By default they are looked up in the texture cache's
# binding memo as Vulkan's EDEN_NX2_BINDMEMO does, and only the ones missed are resolved and
# recorded. The 10 s "Metal binding memo:" line counts both.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_BINDMEMO=0

# Metal renderer: 0 presents every frame as soon as it is ready, as before. By default, with vsync
# and outside the Turbo speed mode, a guest frame is presented no earlier than the game's frame
# period in whole refreshes after the one before (presentDrawable:afterMinimumDuration:), as
# Vulkan's host pacer (EDEN_NX2_HOST_PACE) holds frames: a 30 fps game on a 120 Hz screen shows
# each frame four refreshes. The 10 s "Metal pacing:" line counts the frames held.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_HOST_PACE=0

# Metal renderer: 0 leaves the window's CAMetalLayer without a colour space, as before. By default
# it is tagged sRGB, as MoltenVK tags it for Vulkan's B8G8R8A8_UNORM / SRGB_NONLINEAR swapchain,
# so the display matches the picture's colours (neither renderer outputs HDR).
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_COLORSPACE=0

# Metal renderer: 0 never releases a graphics pipeline, as before. By default, on a memory
# pressure signal from the OS, graphics pipelines no draw took in the last 600 frames are
# destroyed down to the 256 most recent, as Vulkan does on Apple (with
# EDEN_NX2_PIPELINE_EVICT_LEFT_MIB only below that much memory left, fewer and older ones,
# at most EDEN_NX2_PIPELINE_EVICT_MAX). The "Metal: evicted" line says how many.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_PIPELINE_EVICT=0

# Metal renderer: 0 commits a command buffer for every guest fence with work pending, as before.
# By default, with EDEN_NX2_FENCE_FLUSH_US set (phones: 2000), a fence on the GPU thread within
# that many microseconds of the last commit shares the command buffer being recorded: the next
# commit, a fence wait or the GPU thread going idle sends it, as Vulkan's deferred flush. The 10 s
# "Metal fences:" line counts the fences left pending and the idle thread's commits.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_FENCE_BATCH=0

# Metal renderer: 0 draws the display layers with the bilinear or nearest blit whatever the
# scaling filter and anti-aliasing settings say, as before. By default they are applied as on
# Vulkan: FXAA or SMAA over the layer, FSR 1 or SGSR to the screen's size, and the window filters
# (bicubic and its variants, Gaussian, Lanczos, ScaleForce, area, MMPX), with Vulkan's host
# shaders through the translator. The 10 s "Metal present filters:" line counts their passes.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_PRESENT_FILTERS=0

# Metal renderer: 0 lets the game's own DLSS network run where MetalFX does not replace it, as
# before. By default, where the MetalFX Temporal filter is not chosen, MetalFX is unsupported or
# it failed, the game's DLSS is replaced by the Vulkan renderer's temporal stand-in
# (temporal_upscale.frag, then RCAS at the FSR sharpness setting; EDEN_NX2_TEMPORAL_* tune it as
# on Vulkan), as Vulkan does where FSR 3.1 cannot run.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_TEMPORAL_STANDIN=0

# Either renderer: 0 makes the GPU thread's front wait for the GPU and read a compute dispatch's
# size the GPU wrote (Ocarina of Time's light tiles, once a frame). By default it passes
# placeholders on; the dispatch takes its size from the GPU's buffer, and the copy of the size
# the game's macro writes into a constant buffer is made on the GPU (the Metal renderer made no
# such copy before: the constant buffer kept the placeholders).
#EDEN_NX2_INDIRECT_GRID=0

# Threads of a pool of their own ("VkPipelineHeld") for the graphics pipeline builds a draw waits
# for: such a build starts there at once, at the waiting thread's priority (on Apple its QoS
# class), instead of queueing behind the other builds on the low-priority builder pool; a build
# already running there is lent the waiter's QoS (Apple), and the background prebuild pauses while
# a draw waits. 2 by default on Apple, 0 (off, as before) elsewhere.
#EDEN_NX2_PIPELINE_HOLD_BOOST=2

# The list of pipelines a game really drew (what the loading screen builds) is written at most
# this many seconds after a pipeline's first use and when the app leaves the foreground, off the
# GPU thread and through a temporary file. 10 by default on MoltenVK; 0 elsewhere: as before, on a
# first use 15 s after the last save and at shutdown. The Metal renderer reads it for its own
# used list (metal_used.bin, EDEN_NX2_METAL_PIPELINE_FILE): 10 by default, 0 once a minute; it
# also writes its pipeline archive when the app leaves the foreground.
#EDEN_NX2_USED_PIPELINES_SAVE_S=10

# Test: every graphics pipeline built at run time (not at boot or by the prebuild) takes this many
# ms of CPU time longer, to stand in for a slow driver compiler.
#EDEN_NX2_PIPELINE_BUILD_DELAY_MS=300

# Test: threads of the pipeline builder pool, up to the default (logical CPUs - 1; an iPhone 17
# Pro Max has 5).
#EDEN_NX2_PIPELINE_WORKERS=5

# MoltenVK times its compilation stages (SPIR-V to MSL, MSL compile, pipeline compile, ...) for
# the "Perf pipelines:" line. 1 by default on iOS, 0 on macOS.
#EDEN_NX2_MVK_STATS=1

#EDEN_NX2_MME_JIT=0
#EDEN_NX2_SKIP_SAME=0
#EDEN_NX2_INLINE_DEFER=0
#EDEN_NX2_SPLIT_SKIP=1
#EDEN_NX2_AUTO_STUB=1
#EDEN_NX2_KEEP_ASTC=1

# --- Memory ---
# Windows: guest memory is committed as the game allocates it instead of all at start (about
# 4.5 GiB less commit charge in Ocarina of Time). Set to 0 to commit all of it at start.
#EDEN_NX2_SEC_RESERVE=0

# Cap the texture cache's device memory (MiB) below what the graphics driver's budget allows.
#EDEN_NX2_TC_CEILING_MIB=7680

# --- CPU scheduling ---
# Hex mask of guest cores whose host threads keep the top priority (and on Apple the performance
# cores); the others run one class lower. On a 4-CPU host (2 fast + 2 slow, no pinning) Kokiri
# Forest went from 52-53 to 66-70 fps with 03; no change with all 24 CPUs.
#EDEN_NX2_GUEST_CORE_FIRST=03

# Ocarina of Time: 0 keeps the game's own multi-core masks, 2 narrows each to the thread's ideal
# core (default: widened to every core).
#EDEN_NX2_OOT_WIDE_AFFINITY=0

# Yield backoff: a gap between two yields longer than this (us, default 100) starts a new run;
# with 0, changed callee-saved registers no longer start one. Ocarina of Time changes them at
# every yield, so its backoff never sleeps; making it sleep cost about 60 % of the frame rate.
#EDEN_NX2_YIELD_BACKOFF_GAP_US=100
#EDEN_NX2_YIELD_BACKOFF_REGS=0

# "Perf sched:" line (with EDEN_NX2_PERF_REPORT=1): list the busiest n guest threads (default 5).
#EDEN_NX2_PERF_SCHED_THREADS=5
# 0 drops the "Perf threads:" and "Perf sched:" lines and the counting behind them.
#EDEN_NX2_PERF_SCHED=0

# Guest loads/stores that take the JIT's memory callbacks ("Perf memory callbacks:" line).
# arm64 hosts: 1 runs LDXR/STXR in fastmem (a load and a host CAS) instead of a callback each
# (off by default: Ocarina of Time runs none on the PC; iOS Experiments turns it on).
#EDEN_NX2_JIT_INLINE_EXCLUSIVES=1
# A plain load that faults in fastmem gives fastmem up only at its nth fault (default 0 or 1: at
# the first). Read traps fault once and are then disarmed; on the PC phone sim 8 cut Ocarina of
# Time's GPU-tracked slow loads 14k -> 4k/s, but those left are the flushing reads.
#EDEN_NX2_JIT_LOAD_FAULTS=8
# x64, diagnostic: 1 sends LDXR/STXR through the callbacks and the global monitor, as arm64 did.
#EDEN_NX2_JIT_EXCLUSIVE_CALLBACKS=1
# The reactive flushing setting for this session (0 = read traps, as on iOS and macOS).
#EDEN_NX2_REACTIVE_FLUSHING=0
# Guest reads of a page whose GPU-written bytes are not in guest memory yet ("Perf CPU reads:"
# line: asks, cache lock time, waits by cause, who landed the bytes). 0: the GPU thread copies
# the page again and waits for the GPU to go idle, page by page. 1: a fence download of those
# bytes already in flight is waited for (its own submission only) and landed by the GPU thread,
# with the finished downloads within EDEN_NX2_GPU_READ_LAND_KIB (default 256) of the read.
# 2: also, when that download is already submitted, the reading core waits and lands it itself,
# so the GPU thread keeps recording. Default 2 on Apple hosts, 0 elsewhere. PC phone sim, Ocarina
# of Time in Kokiri: GPU thread held 79 -> 49 -> 5.5 ms/s, GPU-tracked load 13.2 -> 9.7 -> 8.2 us.
#EDEN_NX2_GPU_READ_LAND=0
#EDEN_NX2_GPU_READ_LAND_KIB=256
# Hot pages (Djihads80/Eglantine f27522bfb9): a page the guest writes twice within 128 frames,
# each time after an upload had write-protected it, is no longer protected. It counts as written
# at the end of each epoch instead, so its first use in the next epoch uploads it, and the buffer
# cache's write memos (bind skips, uniform reuse, repacked vertex streams) hear of it then. Pages
# the GPU ever wrote are never hot; all hot pages cool down every 128 frames. 0: off. 1: an epoch
# is a frame (as upstream). 2: an epoch also ends with each guest command list. Default 2 on
# Apple hosts, 0 elsewhere. PC phone sim, Ocarina of Time in Kokiri: GPU-tracked guest stores
# 909k -> 439k/s, tracker protections 17.1k -> 9.7k/s, buffer uploads 97 -> 137 MiB/s, frame
# rate unchanged (1: 475k/s, 10.8k/s, 109 MiB/s). Tracker protect and unprotect counts, and the
# hot page counts, are in the "Perf CPU writes:" line.
#EDEN_NX2_HOT_PAGES=0
# Diagnostics: keep the bytes of each hot page upload and compare them at each later use in the
# epoch ("hot verify: stale" = uses write protection would have uploaded first).
#EDEN_NX2_HOT_PAGES_VERIFY=1

# --- Switches the iOS app's Memory & Experiments sets (src/ios_frontend/lichii_bridge_platform.cpp) ---
# An idle guest core polls this long (us) before it blocks (default: the device profile's).
#EDEN_NX2_IDLE_SPIN_US=20

# 0: no zero page trimming of guest memory.
#EDEN_NX2_TRIM_ZERO=0

# 1: the driver's 8-bit indices, MoltenVK too; 0: Lichii widens them on any device.
#EDEN_NX2_UINT8_INDICES=1

# 1: mesh programs writing per-primitive attributes are built natively instead of emulated.
#EDEN_NX2_NATIVE_PER_PRIMITIVE=1

# Texture cache: a render target the game drew in this many frames is freed without a read back
# (0: off); 1: textures that upload again from guest memory are freed first. The iOS device
# profile sets 8 and 1.
#EDEN_NX2_TC_REDRAWN_FRAMES=0
#EDEN_NX2_TC_REUPLOAD_FIRST=0

# arm64 JIT block tables: packed lists (1, iOS profile), per-core fault markers (1: as before),
# compact ranges (0: as before).
#EDEN_NX2_JIT_PACKED_LISTS=0
#EDEN_NX2_JIT_FAULT_LOCAL=1
#EDEN_NX2_JIT_RANGE_COMPACT=0

# Apple: 0 logs no malloc census; 1 also logs one 60 s and 180 s into a game.
#EDEN_NX2_MALLOC_CENSUS=1

# Render passes of at least this many pixels (default 65536, 0: off) begin on a command buffer of
# their own, after one copies can go to instead of ending the pass. KEEP_DEFERRED_CLEAR=0: a
# pass's deferred clear is not kept, as before.
#EDEN_NX2_BEFORE_PASS=0
#EDEN_NX2_KEEP_DEFERRED_CLEAR=0

# Portable JIT-free AArch64 cached interpreter ("cached") or Apple Silicon Hypervisor ("hypervisor").
#EDEN_NX2_CPU_BACKEND=cached
#EDEN_NX2_INTERP_CACHE=0
#EDEN_NX2_INTERP_FUSION=0
#EDEN_NX2_HV_NATIVE_TIMER=1

# Metal present: 1 paces drawables from arrival times instead of the game's requested frame rate;
# 0 draws the 720p applet capture every frame instead of on demand; 0 unswizzles guest-memory
# framebuffers without Switch 2 native GOB tiling.
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_PACE_ARRIVAL=1
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_LAZY_APPLET_CAPTURE=0
#EDEN_NX2_METAL_NATIVE_TILING=0
